methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Athanor is a frontier-tech company in Robotics & Manufacturing at an undisclosed stage. The valuation universe consists of one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. This ten-company peer set provides directional context but lacks density in any narrow cohort.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable. While ten same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, filtering by stage, adjacent-stage positioning, and valuation tier yields fewer than three datapoints in any single bucket. Applying an all-sector median would obscure rather than illuminate valuation, given the heterogeneity of development stage, capital intensity, and commercialization maturity across the peer set. No triangulated valuation range can be derived from the available data without methodological compromise.

A credible valuation for Athanor requires either (1) disclosure of stage and recent financial metrics to enable narrower peer matching, or (2) application of forward-looking methods such as DCF or comparable transaction multiples, neither of which can be anchored without target-specific revenue, growth rate, or M&A precedent data. The current dataset supports descriptive market positioning only: Athanor competes in a sector with meaningful public and private precedent, but insufficient structural alignment prevents quantitative range estimation at this time.
